context: A sortable table of 20 book chapters, each row showing word count, average sentence length, a sparkline of per-sentence word counts, and a mini violin plot of sentence-length distribution — all encoded with a single blue hue and red accent for the longest sentence.
first_impression: Clean and immediately scannable — the table format tames 20 rows of dual mini-charts into a single coherent unit.
what_works: Shared axes across all sparklines and violins enable direct cross-chapter comparison without re-orienting per row; the single-color palette (blue + red accent only) keeps visual search trivial and avoids any legend lookup burden.
what_doesnt: Violin plots at 100×32px are too small to distinguish subtle distributional differences (e.g. slight bimodality vs. skew) — they read as wide-vs-narrow outlines only; sparklines at 140×28px compress enough sentences that individual rhythm patterns within a chapter are hard to trace without hovering.
